plan.notes: Source: official Indiana State University Computer Science department Undergraduate Advising page (https://cs.indstate.edu/web/index.php?title=Undergraduate_Advising), which publishes sample plans of study for each CS concentration. Transcribed verbatim from the department's official file Program_plans_CS_2024.xlsx replacement lineage: the page currently links https://cs.indstate.edu/info/files/Program_plans_CS_2024.xlsx, but that file returns HTTP 404 on the official server (verified 2026-09-30); the latest ACCESSIBLE official version is https://cs.indstate.edu/info/files/Program_plans_CS_2021.xlsx (created 2021-04-15 by CS faculty advisor Jeff Kinne), 'CS BS Computing Sci' sheet: 'CS Computing Science Concentration / 8 semester plan'. Credential verified: the official Indiana State catalog (Department of Mathematics and Computer Science) confers a 'bachelor of science in computer science' with concentrations in computing science, data science, and information science; this plan is the computing-science concentration (the flagship/traditional CS track; data science and information science have separate sheets in the same file). Catalog year set to 2021-2022 from the source file's creation date. Transcription method: manual verbatim transcription of course rows, credits, and printed semester totals from the xlsx sheet. CREDIT-TOTAL CAVEAT: the plan's printed semester totals are 15+17+16+15+15+15+15+14 = 122, while the catalog states the bachelor's degree requires a minimum of 120 credits; total_credits is set to the plan's own published total (122) so the pipeline's exact credit-sum check passes (Clarkson/UVM/GCSU precedent). Prereq arrays are left empty: the plan sheet publishes no per-course prerequisites (it directs students to advisor/MySAM); nothing inferred. CS 499 Senior Design (2 cr) legitimately repeats across Fall Year 4 and Spring Year 4 per the official plan (the catalog confirms students register for CS 499 each of their last two semesters); the Spring instance is coded CS 499-2 with a note. CS 458/L is transcribed exactly as printed (lecture + lab combined, 4 cr). Courses printed without titles (ENG 101, ENG 105) carry the printed text as the title; nothing invented. CURRICULUM-CURRENCY CAVEAT: the CS department's 2025 course-scheduling announcements note that ECT 437 is replacing CS 499 (starting Fall 2025) and CS 210 is being replaced by ECT 373 (information science concentration); students on newer catalog years should confirm with the department. Placement: the catalog requires a math placement examination before registering for an initial MATH class. All CS/MATH courses require a grade of C or better to count in the major.
